brief: Choppy Oct 8 session: S&P -47bps to 7,765, NDX underperformed (-139bps) while R2K (+8bps) and Dow (+10bps) held up; about 70% of S&P constituents actually closed higher, with RTY above SPX above NDX. Two headlines drove the tape: Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the midterms, and a report that OpenAI's annualized revenue is $20bn below prior guidance triggered long-only and hedge fund selling in large-cap tech. That selling combined with weak Samsung/TSM prints, reports that ORCL, AVGO and SCPX plan to tap debt markets further, and a stalled China optical ban hurting COHR/LITE/GLW to drive semis/AI underperformance, widening the S&P-vs-S&P-ex-AI divergence to near 10% over five weeks per GS's baskets team. RTY snapped a 4-day losing streak versus SPX as yields cooled. In derivatives, NDX vol underperformed spot with positioning concentrated in the AI trade, and clients traded GS's SPXXAI (ex-AI) basket to isolate that exposure; GS's hybrids desk flagged a SPXXAI-higher/rates-lower structure as interesting. Elsewhere: Starbucks explored a Chipotle takeover (CMG +8%, SBUX -160bps); healthcare sold off (XLV, ARGX -12%) ahead of Medicare STARs ratings, though HUM rose 12% post-bell on its own STARs results; SpaceX's spectrum purchase hit T/VZ/TMUS after hours.
